name: Striped Attention: Faster Ring Attention for Causal Transformers
problem: Ring Attention's contiguous per-device sequence split creates LOAD IMBALANCE under causal masking: early devices own fewer live tokens than late devices, so the slowest device determines throughput and the whole cluster idles at the end of every step.
mechanism: A simple extension to Ring Attention: instead of contiguous subsequences, each device holds a STRIPE - a subset of tokens distributed UNIFORMLY THROUGHOUT the sequence. Because every device then owns a similar share of every contiguous region, the causal work per device is roughly equal and the pipeline stays balanced.
speedup_reported: Paper's own claims (abstract): up to 1.45x END-TO-END THROUGHPUT improvement over the original Ring Attention on causal transformer TRAINING at sequence length 256K on A100 GPUs and TPUv4s; and 1.65x on 16 TPUv4 chips at sequence length 786K. Hardware and sequence lengths both named. Training-side again, not inference-serving.
